hypothesis: Catalogue inclusion is Selected-At-Random conditional on a small covariate set (local relief, slope, gravity-derived basin-fill proxy, survey coverage, distance to a range front); therefore the omission of true faults from the published compilation is a measurable function of those covariates and can be corrected by inverse-propensity weighting.
mechanism: e(x) = P(S=1 | Y=1, x) is estimated by the SAR-EM recursion of Bekker & Davis (PMLR v94, 2018), as a quantile grid (E1/E2) and as a continuous soft-binned RBF model (E3). Labelled positives carry weight clip(1/e(x), 1, 10) in the propensity-aware empirical risk of Bekker, Robberechts & Davis (arXiv:1809.03207); the matched arm is the same risk with unit weights. Both arms share features, sampler, optimiser, prior and emission rule.
named_non_fault_mimic: Landslide and erosional scarps, paleo-shorelines, lithologic contacts and cultural/roads lineaments in the topographic and gravity-gradient channels: they produce fault-like linear relief without being faults, and they are the reason a raw edge map over-fires.

experiments.instrument: registered: shared gems57.holdout.build_holdout (whole segments withheld uniformly at random per quadrant, 12 px domain erosion, 3 px buffer, 2 seeds x 4 quadrants x {all, detached}) - recorded by the pre-fix writer that did not carry an instrument_note field
experiments.interpretation: The registered instrument withholds whole segments uniformly at random, i.e. it is SCAR by construction: the withheld positives are exchangeable with the visible ones, so there is no covariate-dependent bias to remove and the correction can only add variance. This instrument cannot confirm or refute the selection-bias mechanism.

experiments.instrument: diagnostic instrument: identical geometry/scoring to the shared design but segment withholding probability proportional to (1 - mean e(x))^2
experiments.interpretation: Bias-matched withholding does create the situation the lane exists for, but with the originally published EM scale the fitted propensity was flat (see diagnostics), so the weights were inert.

experiments.instrument: shared gems57.holdout.build_holdout; whole segments withheld uniformly at random inside each quadrant domain
experiments.interpretation: Fixing the pixel-population scale of the EM makes the propensity genuinely non-degenerate, but on the registered SCAR instrument the comparison is still a tie - which is the correct reading of an instrument that contains no selection bias to correct.

experiments.instrument: diagnostic instrument: identical geometry/scoring to the shared design but segment withholding probability proportional to (1 - mean e(x))^2
experiments.interpretation: Duplicate of E3 on the bias-matched instrument; when the withheld set is enriched where the catalogue is thin the comparison is no longer bias-free, and this is the number that tests the mechanism.

gate.rule: pooled blocked-holdout DTI(sar) > DTI(nnpu) overall AND DTI(sar) >= DTI(nnpu) in the highest-propensity tercile, on the pre-registered registered instrument (uniform withholding, blocked folds)
gate.current_holdout_best: NOT ESTABLISHED - no prior holdout artifact exists in this checkout; the matched nnpu arm is the only incumbent available

diagnosis.registered_instrument_is_scar: Uniform segment withholding makes the withheld set exchangeable with the visible set, so no selection bias exists for the correction to remove; E1 and E3 ties are a property of the instrument.
diagnosis.scale_bug_found_and_fixed: The EM originally compared a complete labelled sample with a subsampled unlabeled pool, which lowers the implied hidden-positive mass by exactly the pool ratio (127.7x) and drives the fixed point to e -> 1. With the pixel-population correction the fitted propensity is non-degenerate (E3 diagnostics).
diagnosis.what_remains_unidentified: PU data alone cannot pin the absolute scale of e(x); the lane reports e(x) with an explicit prior convention (pi = catalogue pixel density) and would need a proven exhaustive-completeness source to calibrate it.

correlation_overlap_vs_registry.rule_false_positive: A prior whose own dots cover the whole footprint within 3 px makes the forward-overlap rule trip at ~1.0 for ANY nonempty candidate. The saturation column records that; the rule is only informative against non-saturated priors.
correlation_overlap_vs_registry.scope_note: Prior set = every raster committed in the family's public registry mirror plus explicit extras. Private, unlinked or un-fetched priors are absent; this is a scope-stated check, not proof of global uniqueness.
